items.title: F3DEX2 geometry and state
items.behavior: Digest-admitted F3DEX2 commands cover matrices, viewport, vertices, triangles, lines, lighting, fog, texgen, cull/branch, state DMA, and self-load with loud malformed-command traps.

blockers.detail: Exact reciprocal, transform, clipping-subdivision, line-edge, and negative/boundary fixed-point rounding are not published.
No zero-unsupported representative full-ROM report proves every reached F3DEX2 command/state combination.

items.next_action: Ingest synthetic hardware vectors for fixed-point boundaries, then run admitted F3DEX2 full-ROM task coverage with typed unsupported-event reporting.

blockers.detail: Legacy microcode transform/clipping precision and the historical dedicated quadrangle wire form remain unresolved.
No representative Fast3D/F3DEX-family full-ROM report proves zero reached unsupported commands.

items.next_action: Capture dated/public or hardware evidence for unresolved legacy precision/forms and exercise representative family ROMs through the release report.

items.title: F3DLX.Rej and F3DEX2 Rej/NoN variants
items.behavior: Digest-selected cache sizes and public near-clip/reject-box admission policies are typed without aliasing variant identities.

blockers.detail: F3DLX/F3DLX2 transformed-pixel rounding and exact reject/clipping boundary precision are unknown.
No game-scale report covers the admitted Rej/NoN identities and their reached state combinations.

items.title: L3DEX and L3DEX2 line microcodes
items.behavior: Legacy and modern public line envelopes normalize to typed width, ordered endpoints, clipping, texture/shade attributes, scissor, coverage, blender, and read-only depth behavior.

blockers.detail: Exact microcode transform rounding and silicon line-edge coefficient generation are unmeasured.
No representative L3DEX/L3DEX2 ROM/task corpus demonstrates zero unsupported behavior.

items.next_action: Capture width/endpoint/subpixel edge vectors and add representative line-microcode task coverage.

items.title: S2DEX object and background paths
items.behavior: Digest-admitted S2DEX/S2DEX2 implements typed object loads, rectangles, matrix-relative rectangles, rotating sprites, matrices, composable exact SHRINK/WIDEN perimeter correction, exact inward Average+SHRINK correction on non-rotating rectangle paths, safe-interior Point/Average NOTXCLAMP proofs, status/segment commands, and bounded wrapped point-background strips for declared combinations.

blockers.detail: Public sources do not settle out-of-domain NOTXCLAMP addressing; WIDEN with filtering/flips or inexact quarter-pixel extents; Average with WIDEN or rotating polygons; filtered background neighbour partitions, fractional imageYorig strip rounding, or other perimeter edge ownership. Copy subpixel processing and vertical background subpixel motion are explicitly outside the public supported contract rather than local implementation omissions.
No representative S2DEX full-ROM report proves the implemented subset covers all reached combinations.

items.next_action: Capture repeated hardware vectors for the named perimeter/rounding boundaries, then execute a representative S2DEX full-ROM corpus; do not broaden HLE admission from public intent alone.

items.title: F3DZEX2, Wave, and other game-specific microcodes
items.behavior: These identities remain explicit non-aliasing HLE frontiers rather than being decoded as neighboring public GBIs. Unadmitted graphics images transactionally replay from untouched post-rspboot state through the manual-complete public RSP interpreter, and the accuracy policy can select that LLE path unconditionally before forwarding captured raw DPC work to the renderer.

evidence.needle: The instruction-level model is therefore manual-complete.
## 4. F3DZEX2 remains an explicit unsupported identity

blockers.detail: No allowed complete wire specification currently defines the proprietary family-specific commands.
The public instruction-level RSP model is not cycle-accurate: DMA completes synchronously, pipeline timing is collapsed to instruction boundaries, and exact RSP/RDP overlap remains unmeasured.

No representative F3DZEX2, Wave, or other game-specific full-task corpus proves the LLE path reaches BREAK, commits memory/status, and forwards every reached DRAM/XBUS DPC submission without unsupported behavior.

items.next_action: Run representative F3DZEX2, Wave, and other game-specific full-task corpora through forced LLE with repeated DMEM/RDRAM/DPC evidence; obtain an allowed wire specification only before adding optional typed HLE acceleration.

items.title: Raw DPC command widths and coefficient ingestion
items.behavior: The bounded raw-DPC decoder validates command widths and retains signed edge, shade, texture, and Z coefficients for every public triangle variant without opcode truncation.
items.next_action: Keep every newly admitted raw opcode in the width/coefficient sweep; pixel behavior remains tracked in later rows.

items.title: Ordered RDP state and synchronization commands
items.behavior: Color/depth/texture targets, other modes, tiles/TMEM, fills, and sync commands are retained in display-list order and snapshotted onto emitted work.
items.next_action: Require any new state command to prove ordering, snapshot timing, reset behavior, and loud malformed bounds.

items.title: RSP transform, lighting, fog, and texture generation
items.behavior: Typed matrices, viewport, lighting/look-at, fog alpha, regular/linear texgen, culling, and perspective normalization produce deterministic reference geometry.

blockers.detail: Host-float transforms and analytic texgen do not establish microcode reciprocal/trigonometric table precision or boundary rounding.

items.next_action: Capture reciprocal, matrix accumulation, viewport, clip, lighting half-angle, and texgen lookup boundary vectors.

items.title: One/two-cycle color-combiner routing
items.behavior: All modeled color/alpha mux sources, cycle-zero COMBINED handoff, TEXEL0/TEXEL1, shade, primitive, environment, noise, K4/K5, and LOD fraction feed deterministic combiner equations.

blockers.detail: Silicon accumulator widths, signed negative-product rounding, clamp points, and two-cycle register timing remain unmeasured.

items.next_action: Add raw-DPC hardware vectors around signed products, clamp/tie boundaries, and adjacent-pixel two-cycle register timing.

items.title: YUV conversion and chroma key
items.behavior: Signed K0-K5 conversion coefficients, paired YUV samples, point/filter-convert modes, and key center/scale/width alpha fixup are typed and deterministic.

blockers.detail: Conversion/key accumulator widths, negative rounding, and exact clamp boundaries are not established.

items.next_action: Capture coefficient extrema and negative/tie cases for conversion and key alpha output.

items.title: Framebuffer blender and memory-color feedback
items.behavior: Programmed cycle muxes, fog/pass, force-blend, memory color/coverage, and cycle-one-to-cycle-two handoff produce deterministic framebuffer composites. A strict raw-DPC analyzer preserves a finite 72-point reset-isolated matrix across ordinary/force-blend/fog-pass, one/two-cycle, five-bit alpha extrema/adjacent codes, and exact producer-declared denominator neighbors, plus one command-digest-bound two-adjacent-pixel feedback sequence per mode with raw RGBA/depth/coverage and divergence retained.

evidence.needle: ## Blender precision and adjacent-pixel memory feedback

blockers.detail: The strict final-output analyzer has no reviewed repeated hardware bundles. Five-bit alpha division/rounding, special bypasses, internal cycle-one values, and adjacent-pixel memory-color/coverage timing therefore remain unresolved.

items.next_action: Review the 75-case producer, establish any hidden-coverage prestate in its command prelude, run ten reset-started physical-console captures, and pass repeated-capture consensus before changing blender arithmetic or timing.

items.title: Alpha compare, RGB/alpha dither, and noise
items.behavior: Threshold and dither alpha compare, ordered RGB/alpha patterns before every public color-image format write, disabled RGBA16 truncation, and a seeded per-fragment noise stream are deterministic and share the documented selector topology. Strict capture analyzers preserve complete two-cycle alpha thresholds and isolated 4x4 RGB channel transfer tiles without treating synthetic fixtures as hardware evidence.

evidence.needle: The sample stream is deliberately not claimed

blockers.detail: The silicon random generator, seed/advancement, internal dither precision, and exact alpha-compare ties are unpublished.

items.next_action: Run the typed 1/2-cycle 256-alpha threshold sweep plus per-selector/per-channel 4x4 RGB sweeps on hardware from controlled reset, then add a separate sequence probe if reset does not reproduce one noise sample.

items.title: Compressed Z and hidden DeltaZ storage
items.behavior: Public exponent/mantissa Z encoding, DeltaZ exponent selection, visible/hidden packing, fill-register LSB expansion, decode/encode canonicalization, and inclusive comparison relations are exhaustively tested.
items.next_action: Keep all depth-image imports, fills, and fragment writes on this canonical encoding; unresolved comparison/update precision stays in the raster row.

items.title: Depth source, compare/update, and Z modes
items.behavior: Pixel/primitive depth, fill-register DeltaZ expansion, independent compare/update bits, opaque/interpenetrating/translucent/decal relations, texture rectangles, triangles, and read-only lines share typed depth control. Depth-compared coverage wrap routes through one typed Z-mode decision: opaque selects strict in-front comparison, while interpenetrating wrap traps by name instead of silently aliasing the unsupported adjustment to opaque correlation.

blockers.detail: Exact interpolated Z/DeltaZ quantization, decal/interpenetration boundaries, and the numeric ZMODE_INTER coverage adjustment remain open. The strict 384-point raw-DPC intent/analyzer fixes the admission and stored-coverage denominator, but no reviewed repeated hardware bundle exists; public sources establish when the adjustment is selected but not its arithmetic.

items.next_action: Run the reviewed synthetic producer from reset for the complete ZMODE_INTER matrix on hardware, retain any cycle divergence, pass repeated-capture consensus, and analyze the result before replacing the named trap; separately capture primitive/interpolated Z ties.

items.title: Eight-sample coverage and on-primitive attributes
items.behavior: Raw and high-level triangles retain the public eight-sample checkerboard mask through axis, shared-edge, scissor, preceding-scanline, and one-Q16-LSB boundary sweeps. Full masks evaluate attributes at pixel center; partial masks use one typed bounded-policy covered checkerboard point for shade, texture, and Z. The policy has one explicit total preference order and exhausts every nonzero mask plus every equal-distance tie subset. Strict raw-DPC analyzers preserve all 1,530 mask/cycle/independent-observable selector results and a producer-selected narrow-edge matrix of raw one-LSB-below/on/above accumulator values, exact declared mask/count, and independent shade/texture/depth observations without promoting synthetic fixtures to hardware evidence or encoding a correction formula.

blockers.detail: Programming Manual 15.4 requires on-primitive Z but does not publish the silicon representative-sample lookup, centroid/tie behavior, correction arithmetic, or narrow raw edge accumulator truncation. The strict exhaustive selector and narrow-edge capture intents/analyzers have no reviewed repeated hardware bundles; exact mask and raw accumulator remain producer assertions, and nearest-covered with stable sample-order ties remains a bounded host policy.

items.next_action: Review producers for the 1,530-point selector sweep and the 18-points-per-selected-boundary narrow-edge matrix, run every point from reset on hardware, retain cross-cycle and cross-observable divergence, and pass repeated-capture consensus before deriving or changing any bounded renderer policy.

items.title: Coverage/alpha coupling and memory coverage
items.behavior: All CVG_DST modes, coverage-times-alpha, alpha-coverage select, clear-on-coverage, RGBA16 hidden coverage, RGBA32 memory alpha, and opaque-wrap strict-front behavior are typed. Strict capture analyzers require and preserve the complete 8-coverage by 256-alpha domain in both one-cycle and two-cycle modes for both alpha-product and coverage-to-alpha directions.

blockers.detail: Coverage-times-alpha multiplier width, /255 versus /256 normalization, tie rounding, coverage-to-alpha codes, and same-value hidden-bit writes are unresolved.

items.next_action: Run both complete typed alpha/coverage sweeps through the out-of-tree hardware producer, retain ten-run framebuffer/depth/coverage consensus, and replace only arithmetic supported by those observed curves.

items.behavior: Physical TMEM layout covers odd-row swaps, RGBA32 split banks, YUV planes, block DXT progression, tile origins/fractions, TLUT addressing, and supported RGBA/CI/IA/I decode formats.
items.next_action: Require every new format/load form to add physical-address layout and sampling vectors rather than only decoded colors.

items.title: Texture addressing, filtering, perspective, and LOD
items.behavior: Clamp/wrap/mirror/mask/shift, typed copy-mode clamp bypass, a range-checked signed S10.5 input plus a distinct post-shift host accumulator, point/average/integer-weight three-nearest filters, perspective attributes, YUV convert modes, two-tile cycles, mip/detail/sharpen selection, and LOD fraction share one deterministic sampler. Strict capture analyzers now require reset-isolated one/two-cycle below/on/above matrices for the three-nearest diagonal, reciprocal-to-S10.5 boundary, average-filter output tie, and exact derivative/LOD boundaries across mip/detail/sharpen, with producer-declared numeric controls and framebuffer/depth/coverage observations, without promoting synthetic fixtures to hardware evidence.

blockers.detail: Reciprocal-to-S10.5 rounding, derivative/LOD quantization, average/filter output ties, and silicon filter accumulator width remain open. The strict reciprocal, three-nearest diagonal, average-output-tie, and 18-point derivative/LOD intent/analyzers have no reviewed repeated hardware bundles.

items.next_action: Run reviewed reciprocal-to-S10.5, three-nearest diagonal, average-output-tie, and 18-point mip/detail/sharpen derivative-boundary producers from reset on hardware, retain cycle divergence, and pass repeated-capture consensus; separately capture wider accumulator boundaries before replacing bounded arithmetic.

items.title: Color-image layouts, RDRAM writeback, and hidden bits
items.behavior: Public I8, RGBA16, and RGBA32 layouts share typed import/fill/combined commit paths, pre-write RGB dither, big-endian logical bytes, and physical-address hidden coverage/DeltaZ sidecars. Exhaustive sweeps cover all nine target transitions, all three fill layouts, and the public direct CI8-to-I8 and RGBA16-to-RGBA16 copy pairs while trapping every unsupported pair. Generated-C and typed-Rust CPU halfword stores share one post-commit physical-address event, so an owned RGBA16 sidecar applies the public visible-LSB replication rule even for a same-value write.

blockers.detail: A hardware producer still needs a documented method to observe RGBA16 hidden bits and validate externally produced same-value writes.
No game-scale report proves all reached framebuffer reinterpretation and read/writeback transitions.

items.next_action: Capture hidden-bit results on hardware, then audit reached transitions and event dispositions in full-ROM reports.

items.title: VI restoration, coverage AA, divot, and resampling
items.behavior: The exact public four-value VI STATUS selector admits partial-coverage silhouette AA and resampling for modes 0/1, resampling only for mode 2, and neither for mode 3, while independent DITHER_FILTER admits only full-coverage RGBA16 restoration. Interlaced AA row spacing, divot, and typed register-derived vertical-then-horizontal linear resampling with an explicit held-last border compose deterministically before gamma. A separate strict non-parity digital capture analyzer now preserves the complete 44-point producer-declared active-window, border, insufficient-neighborhood, centroid-candidate, and one-/two-line interlaced-phase matrix with exact source RDRAM/coverage and post-VI bytes; it does not encode a silicon rule.

evidence.needle: ## Digital active-window and neighborhood boundary envelope

blockers.detail: Fixed-point AA/resampling, border fetch, active-window extent, insufficient-neighborhood behavior, centroid selection, half-line phase, field fetch timing, and the mode-0 versus mode-1 extra-line bus-fetch distinction remain unmeasured. The strict digital boundary bundle is only an observation envelope: its synthetic fixture is non-parity, has no hardware-provenance variant, and cannot prove that opaque producer observations correspond to silicon.

items.next_action: Review an external digital-observation producer against the 44-point contract, populate exact reset/retrace-isolated observations without fitting a formula, and independently establish any physical-console provenance before considering renderer changes; separately measure mode-0 versus mode-1 bus-fetch timing.

items.behavior: Integer square-root gamma and seeded stochastic seven-bit quantization provide reproducible digital pre-DAC output with exact endpoint/reference vectors.

blockers.detail: The silicon gamma ROM, random generator, seed/advancement, and exact host-observable quantization mapping are unpublished.

items.next_action: Capture console gamma landmarks and repeated gamma-dither streams with retrace/field provenance.

items.title: VI coverage AA, resampling, field timing, and analog output
items.behavior: No silicon-exact end-to-end VI model currently spans partial-coverage AA through DAC/composite output.

blockers.detail: Active-window extent, exact register/field timing, DAC, and analog encoding are not implemented as one pipeline; coverage AA and H/V resampling remain bounded digital references rather than silicon-exact stages.

The strict analog capture admission program requires a distinct reset-event digest and exact contiguous repeat cohort for every power-cycle run. Comparison v2 additionally binds one cohort-stable extractor, exact source field/sample window, active-output rectangles, and full-active-output alignment, while preserving a non-parity result. The guarded nineteen-vector public NTSC corpus also exists. No ten-run physical-console composite/S-Video cohort, independently reviewed extraction/alignment, or resulting comparison report has been supplied; metadata cannot mechanically prove the physical reset, extraction, or alignment, so unpublished filter/timing details remain unresolved.

items.next_action: Replay the generated public NTSC corpus through ten controlled power-cycle hardware captures per vector/signal with repeat indices 0 through 9 and a distinct observed reset-event digest per run, retain divergent raw outputs honestly, independently review one cohort-stable source field/sample window plus active-output rectangles and full-output alignment, then run comparison v2 without equating a small residual with physical video parity.
